newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria wants locals to take marginal oil fields.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria wants locals to take marginal oil fields.

text.p: New oil guidelines made public on Monday showed Nigeria's military government wants indigenous firms to exploit small, marginal oil fields.

"Marginal fields may be farmed out only to citizens of Nigeria having a company incorporated under the laws of Nigeria," said the guidelines for reallocating the fields issued by the department of petroleum resources and published in the Lagos-based Guardian newspaper.
"Such citizens must be qualified and knowledgeable in the oil industry," it added.
The fields in question are scattered within concession blocks of major oil firms and are estimated to hold minimum recoverable reserves of 800 million barrels but have remained untapped.
The oil majors consider them unprofitable but oil minister Dan Etete has since May been reviewing Nigerian policies to open them for development.
He is backed by the Nigerian Association of Petroleum Engineers, which says development of similar fields in Venezuela, the North Sea and the United States shows Nigeria should not be an exception.

State oil officials said the government was serious about exploiting the marginal fields and making them a preserve of indigenous firms was aimed at bringing Nigerian entrepreneurs into the mainstream of the oil industry, the country's economic lifeblood.

"This is not discrimination. The marginal fields are only a small proportion of an industry which we are really deregulating if you consider the serious decision being taken to privatise our refineries and sell off the joint ventures," one said.
The new guidelines said "The Nigerian entrepreneur may have a foreign technical partner who must not have more than 40 percent equity participation."
Fiscal incentives offered include a petroleum profit tax of 65.75 percent for prospective operators against the existing 85 percent.
But successful applications must develop and produce oil from the fields within five years and also incorporate a plan to utilise the gas from the fields.
Nigeria has proven oil reserves of 20 billion barrels, which are mainly contained in giant fields exploited by multinationals in joint ventures with the Nigerian National Petroleum Corp.
It produces about two million barrels per day (bpd) currently while the national target is to pump 2.5 bpd in 1997 and to raise the national reserves to 25 billion barrels.
